summary: Spacehorse is a space-analog project that maps Earth locations whose environmental conditions most closely resemble Moon and Mars conditions. It uses matched readings such as temperature, radiation, soil moisture, soil water, and atmosphere to compare locations and highlight the best approximate matches. The interface is designed with a NASA-style mission-planning feel, emphasizing location, focus, and base-like exploration. It presents these values as practical, approximate comparisons rather than exact scientific thresholds, making it a useful concept tool for analog site exploration, habitat planning, and futuristic space mission visualization.
details:
What it is:

  • A space-focused web project that explores Earth locations and conditions that could be used as analogy points for Moon and Mars environments.
  • It combines map-like visualization, environmental parameter readings, and a NASA-inspired “location / focus / base” interface concept.

Core goal:

  • Show which Earth coordinates best align with Moon/Mars-like conditions for selected environmental metrics.
  • The project is not trying to claim exact planetary equivalence; instead, it presents the “best approximate matched readings” from supplied data.

Project type:

  • Browser-based front-end with a Node server.
  • The repo includes static HTML pages and a server entry file.
  • This is more of a prototype / interactive data explorer than a production scientific platform.
    • defines the app metadata and Node runtime
    • serves the app
    • likely main landing or map interface
    • contains the key approximate readings and coordinates
    • dashboard-like interface for selecting parameters and viewing matched points
    • likely stores Earth analog site data
    • context file describing NASA-inspired Moon/Mars locations and datasets
    • likely holds data resources used for the visualizations

Important design principle in this project:

  • “Most matched” does not mean “scientifically exact.”
  • The data is treated as a practical approximation for comparison and interface exploration.
  • The UI clearly frames these values as approximate match readings instead of definitive planetary thresholds.

Current improvement status:

  • The repo now reflects this design principle.
  • The matched dataset is explicit and preserved as supplied.
  • The interface focuses on visibility, readability, and interpretation rather than overstating scientific certainty.

Visual concept:

  • mission-control / NASA base feel
  • location-based map presentation
  • parameter-based focus panels
  • selected point details with magnitude and coordinates
  • layered exploration where each metric can be toggled on and off

What the project is trying to communicate:

  • A habitat-planning or exploration-planning analogy:
    • “Which locations on Earth resemble lunar or Martian conditions most closely?”
    • “Which environmental factors matter most for base planning?”
    • “How can we visualize those analog matches cleanly?”

In short:

  • This is a space analog data explorer with a NASA-inspired interface.
  • It is a mock or prototype comparison tool based on approximate matched environmental readings.
  • It is best understood as a storytelling, planning, and visualization project rather than a strict scientific engine.
